notes: The clause לַשֶּׁקֶר עָשָׂה is rendered 'hath wrought falsely': the noun carries 'falsely' and the preposition and its article are left unrepresented under rule 40.

Competing reading worth recording: לַשֶּׁקֶר → 'falsely' also meets rule 30's one-English-word condition, which would make the three morphemes one unit headed on שֶׁקֶר rather than one rendered morpheme beside two unrepresented ones — and that is how JER.8.11 reads עַל־נְקַלָּה → 'slightly'. The accepted reading is kept because rule 12 directs an assimilated article with no written 'the' to unrepresented, and rule 40's subtraction test finds no English word spent on what the לְ contributes.

אֵיכָה has an English word of its own, so the fronted 'do' stays with the verb under rule 17's second limit; the explicit אֲנַחְנוּ takes only 'We' while the copula joins the predicate adjective (rule 20).
עֵט שֶׁקֶר סֹפְרִים is a multi-level chain with no article morpheme: שֶׁקֶר is rendered attributively (rule 28) and the ASV's two supplied 'the's fall on the construct and on the outer rectum.
